evidence.claim: Japan described Russia's actions as a serious violation of international law and the UN Charter and announced sanctions including visa suspensions, asset freezes, and export controls on military-related and dual-use goods.
evidence.title: Sanction Measures following the launch of military actions by Russia in Ukraine (Statement by Foreign Minister HAYASHI Yoshimasa)
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan
evidence.excerpt: Japan described Russia's actions as a serious violation of international law and the UN Charter and announced sanctions including visa suspensions, asset freezes, and export controls on military-related and dual-use goods.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official foreign-ministry sanctions notice that records Japan's state response and legal framing.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Implemented under Kishida's government, though issued by the foreign minister rather than Kishida personally.
contrary_evidence: Sanctions are coercive and align Japan against Russia, but the target is the aggressor state rather than a war of choice by Japan.

evidence.claim: After a North Korean ballistic missile launch, Kishida called the launch outrageous and unacceptable, said Japan would respond immediately, and instructed his government to confirm public safety and maintain the highest readiness while coordinating closely with the United States.
evidence.title: Press Conference by Prime Minister Kishida regarding North Korea's Launch of a Ballistic Missile and Prime Minister Kishida's Thoughts on the First Year of His Administration
evidence.excerpt: After a North Korean ballistic missile launch, Kishida called the launch outrageous and unacceptable, said Japan would respond immediately, and instructed his government to confirm public safety and maintain the highest readiness while coordinating closely with the United States.
evidence.source_locator: Opening remarks on North Korea's missile launch
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official crisis-response statement with immediate operational instructions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Kishida crisis management and alliance coordination.
contrary_evidence: High readiness can be prudent deterrence, but it also reflects a tense security environment rather than pure de-escalation.

evidence.claim: Kishida said the Cabinet approved a new National Security Strategy, National Defense Strategy, and Defense Buildup Program, describing them as a response to a historic crossroads created in part by Russia's aggression against Ukraine.
evidence.title: Press Conference by Prime Minister Kishida
evidence.excerpt: Kishida said the Cabinet approved a new National Security Strategy, National Defense Strategy, and Defense Buildup Program, describing them as a response to a historic crossroads created in part by Russia's aggression against Ukraine.
evidence.source_locator: Opening statement on the three documents
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official cabinet-decision statement by the prime minister on the day of adoption.
contrary_evidence: This is the clearest mixed item: it is lawful defensive security planning, but it also marks a large military buildup that neighbors viewed as escalatory.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Kishida's cabinet endorsed a record 114.4 trillion yen budget and that Kishida's plan to double defense spending to 2% of GDP by 2027 drove a large increase in military outlays.
evidence.title: Japan unveils record budget in boost to military spending
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that Kishida's cabinet endorsed a record 114.4 trillion yen budget and that Kishida's plan to double defense spending to 2% of GDP by 2027 drove a large increase in military outlays.
evidence.source_locator: Opening paragraphs of the Reuters story
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters reporting, syndicated through a major finance outlet, on the scale and political meaning of the budget decision.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly tied to Kishida's cabinet and fiscal priorities.
contrary_evidence: The article frames the move as a response to security challenges, so it is not automatically aggression; it is still a material militarization signal.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Japan approved revisions to three security documents, would acquire a counterstrike capability, and set a target of doubling annual defense spending to about 2% of GDP, while China denounced the move.
evidence.title: U.S. hails Japan's new security strategy as China lashes out over moves
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that Japan approved revisions to three security documents, would acquire a counterstrike capability, and set a target of doubling annual defense spending to about 2% of GDP, while China denounced the move.
evidence.source_locator: Opening paragraphs of the Reuters report
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent Reuters report on the international reaction to Kishida's security shift.
evidence.period_fit: Immediate aftermath of the December 2022 security decision
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct consequence of Kishida cabinet policy, though presented through external reaction.
contrary_evidence: The China backlash is evidence of perceived escalation by neighbors, not proof of unlawful aggression.

unresolved_gaps: Stronger direct evidence of Kishida's personal control over police, prosecutors, and protective institutions before and after the Abe assassination.
More evidence that the church-scandal and protest responses reduced actual harm rather than only improving the public narrative.
More independent evidence that the 2022 growth/distribution package actually changed household welfare or investment outcomes rather than only announcing them.
Better separation of Kishida's policy effect from BOJ policy, exchange-rate moves, and imported inflation shocks.
Direct year-end outcome evidence for child, fertility, and social-service gains attributable to the 2022 package.
More subgroup evidence on single-parent households, disabled people, housing insecurity, and food insecurity.
Direct, traceable evidence of Kishida's own assets, private interests, donor links, or personal self-enrichment is missing.
Independent corroboration of the personal claim that Kishida had no links to the former Unification Church and that his vetting instructions were fully followed.
More independent evidence on whether the 2022 startup, digital, and green-growth agenda actually produced measurable execution, not just planning.
Clearer separation of Kishida's own execution from external shocks and inherited macro conditions when judging the economic package and wage trajectory.
